subject: Risk closure snapshot and SLA acknowledgement for remediation tempo
messages:
From: Timothy Barnes <timothy.barnes@fintechco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: audits@brightaudit.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: snapshot of vulnerability closure tempo + SLA acknowledgement

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG/SOC2 evidence collection we need a short "closure snapshot" covering your current vulnerability management tempo:
- average time-to-remediate (TTR) for P1/P2 in the last 90 days
- what patch windows and emergency rollback processes are in place
- any exceptions or SLA deviations for the last quarter and owner for each

Can you also confirm whether Redwood will commit to the following for our SIG response:
- P1 CVE remediation target: 72 hours to mitigation plan, 30 days to fix or mitigate with compensating control
- P2: 14 calendar days

We prefer a single PDF/CSV bundle we can upload to our audit portal. If you can attach the snapshot + POAM and a short attestation that the above targets reflect your current operational commitment, that would be ideal.

Let me know if you need anything from our side (e.g., a list of CVEs we care about or exceptions that matter to us).

—Timothy
Lead Security Engineer, FinTechCo

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Barnes <timothy.barnes@fintechco.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: snapshot of vulnerability closure tempo + SLA acknowledgement

Timothy —

Appreciate the clear ask. We're preparing a compact evidence packet. Quick notes up front:
- We run continuous authenticated scans (Qualys) plus nightly image-level scans and weekly container layer scans.
- Typical remediation tempo (rolling 90-day median): P1 = 48 hours to mitigation plan, P2 = 9 days to remediation.
- Emergency patch windows: immediate 24–72 hour window with mandatory postmortem for any rollback.

We'll attach:
1) small CSV export with TTR metrics by severity for the last 90 days
2) POAM PDF that lists owners, escalation chain, and planned close dates
3) a 1-page attestation signed by Security Ops that restates the tempo and SLAs you listed (we can accept a slight wording tweak to match Redwood ops language).

Question: do you require a notarized signature or is an electronically-signed attestation sufficient for BrightAudit?

I'll loop Laura (security compliance) and Monica (ops) on logistics. Expect the packet within EOD PDT.

—Marcus
Head of Reliability & Security Operations, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Barnes <timothy.barnes@fintechco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: snapshot of vulnerability closure tempo + SLA acknowledgement

Timothy —

BrightAudit has handled electronic attestations in the past; we don't need a wet signature unless the customer portal explicitly requires it. Monica will attach the POAM and a CSV export of our Qualys summary.

Two clarifications:
- For P1 we commit to 72 hours to mitigation plan in customer-facing language; internally our target remains a 48-hour median for plan creation. The attestation will say "Redwood commits to providing a mitigation plan for P1 CVEs within 72 hours of detection/triage for customer records."
- Exceptions: any remediation that requires third-party vendor fixes (upstream dependency) will be listed in the POAM and marked as "vendor-dependent" with an estimated SLA and owner.

We'll include the following attachments: redwood_vm_snapshot-march2028.csv, poam-tempo-commitment.pdf, screenshot-qualys-summary.png

—Laura
Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: BrightAudit Team <audits@brightaudit.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: snapshot of vulnerability closure tempo + SLA acknowledgement

Thanks — received the note. For our SOC2 work we prefer: (a) a CSV with one row per CVE showing date detected, severity, mitigation plan date, remediation date (if closed), and owner; and (b) the POAM with a column showing expected close date and current status. The PDF attestation can be appended to the POAM.

If Redwood can provide the CSV + POAM by COB Monday PST, that's fine for our timeline. Also, please include a short bullet on how you handle backporting patches for managed DB images (we'll tag that as "managed infra" in the auditor portal).

Regards,
BrightAudit Team

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Barnes <timothy.barnes@fintechco.com>, BrightAudit Team <audits@brightaudit.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 16 Mar 2028 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: snapshot of vulnerability closure tempo + SLA acknowledgement

Hi all —

Attached is the packet we discussed. Short summary inside the CSV and POAM:
- 90-day median TTR: P1 = 48 hours (mitigation plan within 72 hours for customers), P2 = 9 days
- 6 open vendor-dependent items are tracked in the POAM with expected vendor ETA column populated
- Backporting for managed DB images: we run staged backports; emergency backport path exists and is used for P1s (process described in POAM appendix B)

Attachments (included): redwood_vm_snapshot-march2028.csv, poam-tempo-commitment.pdf, screenshot-qualys-summary.png

If you need a signed cover letter for the portal, we can produce an electronically-signed attestation and a timestamped PDF. Let us know which format you prefer and we will upload to the Drive link shared earlier.

Thanks — Monica
Security Operations Program Manager, Redwood Inference
